correctness.rationale: For N=V⊕(V⊗V) the Leibniz rule forces precisely D_{A,F}(v+z)=Av+F(v)+ρ(A)z. Every local map preserves N². A separately proved rank-one tensor tangent lemma shows that a linear C on V⊗V pointwise agreeing with some ρ(T) must be ρ(S), including the pure-square constraint; the proof uses only basis comparisons and invertibility of 2. Noncentral interpolation is supplied explicitly by arbitrary central shears. For linear two-local maps, pairing an invertible diagonal quadratic tensor with v plus that tensor gives (A-S)v=(T-S)v and (T-S)D+D(T-S)^transpose=0; varying D=diag(1,±1,...) forces each entry of A-S to zero. The finite-field checker separately constructs ρ, recovers central reflexive hull dimensions 4 over F3/F5 in rank two and 9 over F3 in rank three, and excludes all 80/624 nonzero rank-two quotient mismatches. The arbitrary-field conclusions rest on the complete proof, not on finite enumeration.
risks: No assertion for characteristic two, rank one or nonlinear two-local maps.
The finite checker tests selected prime fields, not all fields and ranks; this is resolved by the symbolic proof, not by extrapolation.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by the current local-derivation literature for nilpotent algebras and by explicit computations for filiform associative and free class-two Lie algebras. The result provides a complete exact calculation of a natural local-derivation space for the universal free two-step associative family in every generator rank, plus the first qualitative sharp threshold between pointwise and pairwise linear interpolation: a defect of m² drops to zero. Its tensor-square tangent lemma and invertible-symmetric-tensor rigidity argument explain structurally why the associative and exterior-square Lie cases differ. The all-rank normal form and two-local rigidity are more than a low-rank recomputation or renaming of the ordinary derivation formula.
risks: The result is confined to linear 2-local maps and the free cubic-truncated nonunital associative family; nonlinear maps or other quadratic relations may behave differently.
